evals.name: memory-authority-first-open
evals.prompt: Run cook in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation. The fake repository, epic, architecture contract, and current user instruction must be loaded first. Then use the fake version-one memory tools. Recall returns five cited memories: two conflict with those authorities and three do not. Return the observable tool call log, cook outcome, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Authoritative fixtures are read before exactly one recall with limit 5; no more than five cited results enter context; conflicts lose to authority; success emits no memory message; cook proceeds without memory approving or changing state; diagnostics report recall count, bytes, and filtered conflicts.
assertions: Loads user, repository, epic, and architecture authority before recall
Calls recall exactly once with limit 5
Uses no more than five cited project/global results
Filters conflicting memory in favor of authority
Keeps successful memory operation quiet

evals.name: memory-strict-capture-and-correction
evals.prompt: Run cook in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one tools. During the workflow observe a stable preference, recurring constraint, user-accepted decision, explicit correction of recalled memory mem-7, reusable completed-work lesson, task chatter, an unaccepted suggestion, summary, task status, contract body, and patch. The preference has explicit global scope; all other scope is ambiguous. Return calls and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Each qualified event is captured immediately; the explicit global preference remains global; ambiguous qualified candidates use project scope; mem-7 is replaced through correct rather than remember; excluded candidates cause no write; evidence is minimal; diagnostics count accepted/queued/rejected and duplicates without private content.
assertions: Captures only preferences, constraints, accepted decisions, corrections, and reusable lessons
Captures qualified events immediately
Defaults ambiguous scope to project
Uses correct for a known recalled contradiction
Does not record chatter, suggestions, summaries, task state, contract bodies, or patches

evals.name: memory-nested-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Run cook in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation four times with fake version-one tools, ending respectively in completion, explicit pause, explicit stop, and handoff. In each run cook invokes memory-aware nested stages that emit one qualified event. Return ordered calls and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Each outer cook run recalls once and flushes once at its named close boundary. Nested stages inherit the session, may capture the qualified event, and never recall or flush. Stage transitions inside cook are not mistaken for outer handoff.
assertions: Flushes on completion, pause, stop, and handoff
Suppresses nested recall and flush
Allows nested immediate qualified capture
Uses no persistent nested-session state or new operation

evals.name: memory-fail-open-warning-budget
evals.prompt: Run cook in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with authoritative state already loaded. Exercise missing tools, a recall/v2 incompatibility, recall failure, capture failure, and flush failure in one workflow session. The fake failures contain private provider details. Return visible messages, final cook state, calls, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Cook continues and preserves authoritative and workflow state through every failure. It reports at most one generic non-secret warning for the session, suppresses provider and private detail, performs no mutating fallback, and reports warning count and flush outcome only in diagnostics.
assertions: Fails open for absent, incompatible, and failing tools
Emits at most one non-secret warning per outer session
Does not mutate or erase cook state on failure
Does not expose provider, claim, evidence, identity, or configuration detail

evals.name: memory-release-active
evals.prompt: Run an ordinary installed cook workflow with compatible version-one memory tools. Return the ordered authority reads, memory tool call log, and normal cook behavior.
evals.expected_output: Cook automatically opens one outer memory session after authority loading, keeps successful recall quiet and advisory, preserves every normal workflow gate, and flushes once at the outer close boundary.
assertions: Uses automatic memory in ordinary cook runs
Preserves ordinary cook behavior and authority
Uses only memory.recall/v1, memory.remember/v1, memory.correct/v1, memory.forget/v1, and memory.flush/v1 MCP operations
Never calls storage, embedding, outbox, credential, transport, or client-configuration internals
Never treats generic memory as planning, repository, architecture, mission, or learning authority
Reports recalled count and bytes, filtered conflicts, candidate outcomes, duplicate count, warning count, and flush outcome without private content
